text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Arafat knew of World Trade Center plot, deputy defence minister Peled charges
- Fatah plans Land Day "power" demonstrations
- Nature lovers ignore Green Line
- Clashes continue in territories
- Dagan: Terrorists may strike soon
- Netanyahu, Peres deny unity government deal
HAARETZ
- Senior intelligence officer: Arafat decided to abandon peace process, use violence
- Sources close to Netanyahu: the PM knows he cannot move towards peace with current government
- Police: if necessary we will investigate rabbi Ovadia Yossef
- Migdal insurance rejects demand to fire directors over cartel convictions
- Military sources: Rajoub inciting demonstrations, attacks
- Fear in treasury liberalisation of foreign currency can cause escape of capital and devaluation
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Israel: the U.S. should "bend" Arafat
- Army chief: if the Palestinians use violence it is war
- Bank Leumi to give bonuses to all workers after furore over bonuses to seniors
- Hamas's Maqadmeh arrested
- President Weizman offers help in forming unity government
MAARIV
- Attempted terrorist attacks foiled in recent days
- Security officials warn tension high
- Diplomatic efforts to prevent further attacks
- Insurance companies delay decision on directors convicted of forming cartel
GLOBES
- Finance Minister: team examining raising retirement age to 67 for men, 62 for women
- Offer of some $200 million as foreign exchange resumes, Israel Bank intervenes
- State: attorney Avi-Yitzhak has much evidence on Bar-On affair
